Gap_Title: Adversarial Abort vs. Non-Adversarial Autonomous Recovery in Space PQC
Problem_Statement: Cryptographic fault defenses mandate immediate abort to prevent side-channel leakage (SIFA/DFA), while space avionics operate in non-adversarial cosmic ray environments where aborting decapsulation drops critical commands or telemetry, causing mission desynchronization.
Evidence_from_Literature: Dobraunig et al. (TCHES 2018), Ravi et al. (TCHES 2023), Kim (Acta Astronautica 2026), Dodd & Massengill (IEEE TNS 2003)
Closest_Existing_Approaches: Paul et al. (ACM TECS 2024), Sarker et al. (IEEE TCSI 2023), Hermelink et al. (INDOCRYPT 2021) - all use detection-only abort
Unaddressed_Limitations: Existing PQC defenses provide no autonomous arithmetic recovery; aborting drops availability; no evaluation of availability vs. side-channel leakage trade-off
Candidate_Research_Question: Can in-place algebraic rollback achieve autonomous recovery for radiation-induced arithmetic SEUs in ML-KEM without opening statistical ineffective fault attack (SIFA) side-channels?
Proposed_Technical_Contribution: In-place butterfly rollback mechanism for ML-KEM decapsulation combining local transient recovery with fail-stop implicit rejection and formal constant-time validation
Feasible_Experimental_Methodology: Fault-injection campaign comparing transient SEU recovery rate, silent data corruption, and constant-time statistical timing ratios (Welch t-test, Cohen d)
Baselines_and_Metrics: Baselines: Unprotected FIPS 203, Abort-on-fault, Software DMR. Metrics: Recovery rate, P_SDC, Latency overhead, Timing ratio
Main_Risks_and_Novelty_Threats: Risk: Reviewers might argue that recomputation in cryptography is fundamentally risky under active physical attacks; must clearly bound threat model to space cosmic rays
Confidence_Level_and_Classification: HIGH (New inference from comparing aerospace dependability with cryptographic fault literature)

Gap_Title: Cross-Layer Coordination of Endpoint PQC Recovery with Link-Layer Error Control
Problem_Statement: Space communication protocols (DTN, CCSDS, NTN) assume radiation faults only corrupt the wireless channel, while PQC implementations assume perfect channels. Endpoint decapsulation SEUs trigger implicit rejection, misdiagnosed as RF fades and causing unnecessary, costly space-link retransmissions.
Evidence_from_Literature: El Bizri et al. (IEEE ICC 2026), Elewaily et al. (Ad Hoc Networks 2024), RFC 9171 / 9172, CCSDS 734.1-B-1
Closest_Existing_Approaches: El Bizri et al. (channel-adaptive PQC for NTN, but assumes 100% fault-free hardware); Elewaily et al. (DTN custody transfer, ignores crypto SEUs)
Unaddressed_Limitations: Zero coordination between endpoint cryptographic health status and link-layer FEC/ARQ adaptation; RF fades and computational SEUs are conflated
Candidate_Research_Question: How does cross-layer coordination between in-tree PQC fault status and link-layer erasure coding affect goodput and retransmission overhead in simulated space links?
Proposed_Technical_Contribution: A cross-layer telemetry bus and adaptive controller coupling ML-KEM endpoint health tokens with Reed-Solomon erasure coding and interleaving over a Markov channel
Feasible_Experimental_Methodology: Simulate discrete-event space link (Gilbert-Elliott DTMC, 10ms-250ms RTT) with simultaneous RF channel fades and endpoint ALU/memory fault injection
Baselines_and_Metrics: Baselines: Uncoordinated PQC + Static FEC, Hardware DMR, Channel-only adaptive FEC. Metrics: Unnecessary retransmissions, Goodput, P_SDC, Transaction latency
Main_Risks_and_Novelty_Threats: Risk: Implementation complexity of full communication stack; risk of scope creep beyond final-year timeline; requires rigorous discrete simulation
Confidence_Level_and_Classification: MODERATE (New inference from comparing satellite communication protocols with cryptographic fault behavior)

Gap_Title: Complete Dual-Transform (Fwd + Inv) NTT Monitoring on Embedded Space Processors
Problem_Statement: Published NTT error detection focuses almost exclusively on hardware FPGAs and covers only Forward NTT. In software on space-grade embedded architectures (RISC-V, LEON3), Inverse NTT (45% of decapsulation butterflies) is unmonitored, and compiler methods double register pressure.
Evidence_from_Literature: Paul et al. (ACM TECS 2024), Sarker et al. (IEEE TCSI 2023), Reis et al. (CGO 2005), Fritzmann et al. (IEEE Access 2020)
Closest_Existing_Approaches: Paul et al. (FPGA Forward NTT only); Sarker et al. (ASIC Forward NTT only); SWIFT/EDDI (generic compiler duplication)
Unaddressed_Limitations: Inverse NTT is unmonitored in published algebraic checks; hardware FPGA designs cannot be directly deployed on microcontroller/processor flight software
Candidate_Research_Question: What is the minimal-overhead algebraic invariant formulation that achieves 100% butterfly coverage for combined forward and inverse NTT in software on embedded space cores?
Proposed_Technical_Contribution: Formulation and implementation of dual-transform complementary invariants (CT-NTT sum/diff + GS-InvNTT sum/mult) optimized for embedded C on RISC-V/SPARC
Feasible_Experimental_Methodology: Cross-compile and execute on QEMU-emulated space processors (LEON3 / RISC-V RV32IM); evaluate instruction count, register spills, and fault coverage
Baselines_and_Metrics: Baselines: Clean native code, SWIFT instruction duplication, Software DMR. Metrics: CPU cycle overhead, code size, register pressure, fault detection coverage
Main_Risks_and_Novelty_Threats: Risk: Perceived as an incremental extension of Paul et al. to software and inverse NTT; must emphasize novel dual-transform mathematical derivation

Gap_Title: Radiation-Informed Physical Fault Modeling vs. Arbitrary Pseudo-Random Fault Injection for PQC
Problem_Statement: Cryptographic fault testing almost universally uses uniform pseudo-random bit flips across memory arrays. Space radiation physics exhibits distinct non-uniformities: heavy-ion LET thresholds, Multi-Cell Upset (MCU) topological clusters, and Poisson arrival distributions.
Evidence_from_Literature: Dodd & Massengill (IEEE TNS 2003), ECSS-Q-ST-60-15C, NASA-HDBK-4002A, Hsueh et al. (IEEE Computer 1997)
Closest_Existing_Approaches: Standard uniform random fault injectors (Engineered random bit flipping in software); Hardware beam testing (expensive, non-reproducible software access)
Unaddressed_Limitations: Existing PQC fault literature evaluates against unphysical fault distributions; lacks orbit-specific flux rate mapping and physical cluster modeling
Candidate_Research_Question: How do orbit-informed radiation fault models (LET spectra, MCU cluster geometries, Poisson arrival rates) alter the observed vulnerability and recovery of ML-KEM software?
Proposed_Technical_Contribution: A physics-informed software fault injection framework for PQC implementing CREME96/ECSS-calibrated Poisson SEU arrival and 2D/3D MCU cluster models
Feasible_Experimental_Methodology: Develop a calibrated fault injection module translating LEO (ISS/polar) and GEO orbit radiation profiles into discrete-event software execution upsets in ML-KEM
Baselines_and_Metrics: Baselines: Uniform pseudo-random bit flipping, Single-bit SEU only. Metrics: Vulnerability surface, Masking probability, SDC rate under clustered vs. independent faults
Main_Risks_and_Novelty_Threats: Risk: Requires convincing aerospace reviewers of the validity of software-level abstraction of nuclear physics; does not provide physical beam validation
Confidence_Level_and_Classification: HIGH (Explicitly acknowledged gap in testing methodology)
